variables.reason: The typed ledger defines Ra as the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations (arithmetic mean roughness). The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness has symbol Ra/R_a, canonical quantity arithmetic mean roughness, and definition 'Mean absolute deviation of surface height from its mean level', which is exactly the ledger definition. Its si_dimension is L with dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0], supporting every nonzero coordinate (L=1) in the candidate. The record therefore applies directly to the ledger variable Ra and justifies the dimensional vector.

The ledger defines kt as peak-to-valley height (vertical distance between highest peak and lowest valley). The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height gives the same canonical quantity (mean peak-to-valley roughness height) with si_dimension L and dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0], explicitly noting any height difference retains length dimension. That record directly matches the typed definition and supports the candidate L=1 vector.

The ledger defines k_rms as root-mean-square height (RMS of height deviations). The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height describes the root-mean-square roughness height, with si_dimension L and dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]. This canonical entry corresponds to the ledger variable and confirms the length dimension (L=1) for k_rms.

The ledger defines Sk as the skewness of roughness height fluctuations (a standardized third moment). The KB record pq_height_skewness gives surface-height skewness as the third standardized moment and explicitly lists si_dimension 1 with dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0]. This record matches the ledger definition and supports all coordinates (all zero) in the candidate vector.

The ledger defines Ku as the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations (standardized fourth moment). The KB record pq_height_kurtosis corresponds to surface-height kurtosis, listed as a dimensionless standardized moment with dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0]. This canonical record directly applies and supports the candidate dimensionless vector.

The ledger defines ES as the effective streamwise slope (mean absolute gradient of surface height in flow direction). The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope gives the same quantity with definition 'Mean absolute gradient of surface height in a specified horizontal direction' and explicitly notes a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is dimensionless. Its dimension_vector is [0,0,0,0,0,0,0], which supports the candidate all-zero vector for ES.

The ledger defines Po as surface porosity (fraction of surface area occupied by voids). The KB record pq_porosity defines porosity/void fraction as a dimensionless fraction with dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0], matching the ledger variable definition and supporting the candidate dimensionless vector.
